title: Federated Continual Graph Learning

problem.claim: Evolving graph data creates storage and privacy challenges, while continual GNN training can cause catastrophic forgetting of earlier tasks.

gap.claim: Existing continual graph learning methods rely on centralized architectures and do not leverage distributed graph databases for collective intelligence.

contributions.claim: Federated Continual Graph Learning adapts GNNs across multiple evolving graphs under storage and privacy constraints.

POWER preserves experience nodes with maximum local-global coverage to mitigate local graph forgetting and uses pseudo-prototype reconstruction with trajectory-aware knowledge transfer to address global expertise conflict.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The empirical study identifies local graph forgetting and global expertise conflict as core challenges.
Experiments on various graph datasets reportedly show that POWER outperforms federated adaptations of continual graph learning baselines and vision-centric federated continual learning approaches.

narrative_sequence.summary: Evolving graph data creates storage and privacy challenges, and continual GNN training can cause catastrophic forgetting.
Existing continual graph learning methods are centralized and overlook distributed graph databases.
The study identifies local graph forgetting and global expertise conflict as challenges in federated continual graph learning.
POWER addresses these challenges through experience-node preservation, pseudo-prototype reconstruction, and trajectory-aware knowledge transfer.
Experiments on various graph datasets reportedly show POWER outperforming specified baseline families.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates client-side local graph forgetting from server-side global expertise conflict.

interpretation.claim: Federated continual learning may require distinct mechanisms for local retention and cross-client aggregation conflicts.

application.claim: When designing federated continual systems, diagnose forgetting and aggregation conflict as separate failure modes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation generalizes beyond the studied graph-learning setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the graph datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details or computational and communication costs of POWER.
